newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bonds end mixed, unlinked bonds fall.
newsitem.headline: Israel bonds end mixed, unlinked bonds fall.

text.p: Israeli bond prices closed mixed as inflation-linked bonds continued to rise while unlinked issues except Makams fell in fairly active trading, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): -0.1 pct to 166.85
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.1 pct at 158.56

Volume was strong at 160 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in unlinked bonds. Issues such as Gilon posted medium declines on profit-taking after recent strong rises, traders said.
In contrast, Makams, which are also unlinked, rose on heavy demand. "Makams are giving good yields of about 15.5 to 15.6 percent," said Roy Meir, managing director of Simodan.
Long bonds linked to the consumer price index (CPI) gained, continuing the trend of the past two months. Yields have now fallen from a peak of 5.2 percent to 4.6 percent.
"They have strengthened on news that provident funds are very liquid as public redemptions have fallen," said Alon Kaufman, investment manager at Meitav Investments.
Provident funds, long-term savings funds with special tax benefits, prefer to invest in linked bonds.
Kaufman also noted that their supply has shrunk as recent government issues have tended toward unlinked bonds.
Dollar-linked bonds held steady in thin volume as the shekel weakened mildly. The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2510 shekels against 3.2560 on Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
